results.reason: Issue 1 identifies that MSA § 3.2 grants nationwide exclusivity over all warehousing, freight and delivery services. It contrasts this with Term Sheet § 4.1, which limits exclusivity to NYC-metro last-mile delivery, and proposes replacement language narrowed to that scope.

Issue 2 explains that § 11.3 makes Customer's § 10.2 indemnity unlimited while Provider's § 10.1 indemnity stays subject to the 12-month cap. It describes the one-sided exposure and recommends striking the carve-out and making the exceptions mutual.

Issue 3 identifies that DPA § 9.1 selects Delaware law and Wilmington courts, in conflict with MSA § 18.1. It states that the DPA prevails under § 2.3 and recommends conforming the DPA to New York law and forum.
Issue 4 identifies the 3-year auto-renewal and the 15-day notice window, and explains the lock-in risk. It recommends 1-year renewals with notice at any time at least 90 days before expiry.

Issue 5 identifies that SOW § 8.2 allows assignment without Customer's consent while MSA § 17.4 restricts only Customer. It explains the risk of transfer to a competitor or unvetted carrier and recommends a mutual consent requirement.
The memo states that the DPA prevails over the MSA, and the MSA over the SOW, under § 2.3.
The memo states that the § 11.1 cap is the fees paid or payable in the 12 months before the claim.
The response is a memorandum addressed to the Supervising Partner. Each issue gives the document and section (Where), Why it matters, and a Recommended fix.
The issues are listed in order of importance, and Section V lists items to raise with the client before the next turn.
The memo states that the Delaware clause controls data disputes and that the documents are not consistent on governing law.
The memo states that the exclusivity clause is far broader than the Term Sheet and contradicts it.
